source_problem.original_order: src/nvidia/arch/nvalloc/unix/src/osinit.c: rm_shutdown_adapter destroys engine state before late kgspUnload; original engine frees can occur after controller drain while GSP still runs.
source_problem.logical_unmap: src/nvidia/arch/nvalloc/unix/src/os.c:4099-4146; successful nv_dma_unmap_alloc revokes original logical mapping metadata.
source_problem.consequence: IRQ exclusion does not prove hardware DMA stopped. Physical pages and exact retained IOVA must survive those logical frees until independent positive original shutdown proof.

entry_contract.timing: The ordinary-thread serialized owner calls this before any original adapter entry that may start GPU DMA, after exact RM binding. Beginning is conservative retention, never a hardware readiness claim.
entry_contract.identity: Capture exact bound nv_state pointer, Session identity and new globally unique nonzero generation; a repeated begin while held refuses without replacing them.

stop_contract.fixed_verifier: NV_STATUS s540GspContextValidateDmaStopReceipt(const void *originalState, const void *sessionIdentity, NvU64 sessionGeneration, const S540GspDmaStopReceipt *receipt);
stop_contract.production_dependency: Strong direct reference to the original Context bridge. No weak import, caller callback, caller-populated structure or Boolean can clear the hold.
stop_contract.receipt: Opaque type owned by the reviewed original bridge; transport never constructs or dereferences it. Verification must match exact original state, Session and generation and positively prove original GSP/adapter teardown.
stop_contract.failure: Missing, foreign, stale, failed or unissued proof preserves every page, IOVA, binding and lifetime hold. A successful proof cannot be replayed to clear a newer generation.
stop_contract.active_ten_overlay_profile: The actual Context bridge has no issuer and returns NV_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. A begun lifetime therefore remains retained; the operational owner gate stays blocked. A prospective checked teardown patch is not active-profile proof.

reclamation: Both independent conditions are required: every attempted IRQ enable has successfully drained AND a begun hardware-DMA lifetime has an accepted matching stop receipt.
nv_free_pages and nv_dma_unmap_alloc acknowledge exact logical per-allocation retirement while either condition remains unproved, retaining original physical backing, command and IOVA.
Final nv_free_kernel_mapping closure obeys the same rule; CPU aliases retain their legitimate token identity until close and cannot trigger early backing release.
Generic Session::release/unmapDma cannot bypass the hold. Private physical release and registry drain check both conditions too, even if the retirement registry is empty.
Unbinding or stopping the Session refuses while the hardware lifetime is held. Backend completion failure after proof retains progress and owners for retry/quarantine.
The owner obtains original stop proof, confirms it, then drains retirement before Context destruction/unbinding. Controller drain alone is never a stop proof.

native_evidence.fixture_scope: Native-only sealed mock authority, rejected at compile time under KERNEL; absent/unissued receipts refuse. It never supplies a production receipt or executes original GPU teardown.
coverage: Logical unmap and engine free after IRQ teardown retain pages and exact IOVA while GSP lifetime is held.
Final CPU alias close retains backing; generic free/unmap and owner unbind/stop cannot bypass retention.
Null, unissued, foreign-state, foreign-Session, stale-generation, failed and still-running receipts refuse without reclamation.
Hardware proof before IRQ drain still cannot reclaim, and IRQ drain before hardware proof still cannot reclaim.
Never-armed failed-init lifetime and empty registry still need a matching positive receipt; successful old receipts cannot clear a new generation.
Unpublished failed mapping constructors may clean up their new command, while failed retained-map revalidation after IRQ drain never tears down old IOVA.
